docs.title: Welcome to Heimdall
docs.text:
A CLI to help with your git directories (for now 😉).

Based on the myth of the Nordic God, Heimdall, the CLI is here to ease with your multiple Git repositories.

For now, Heimdall has 2 main commands :

  • Git-info to help you manage all your git repositories and now their current branch, if they have some local changes or if they are behind the remote repository
  • Git-clone to clone a git repository and keep the same path

Run without any command, Heimdall opens a TUI to navigate through your git repositories and run actions on one or several of them.

docs.title: How to install
docs.text:
On MacOS:

Heimdall is available through brew

brew tap yodamad/tools
brew install heimdall

On Linux: ⚠️ Use it at your own risk for now ⚠️

There are available on Release page but not well tested to be honest

On Windows: ❌ Not available for now, some compatibilities problems.

WSL2 option

It works with the linux version

docs.title: How to configure
docs.text:
All the configuration elements are detailed in the configuration file section.

You can override this value with the --config-file or -f flag defined in the global flags.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
This file has to be a yaml formatted file.

In this config file, you can configure these elements in three ways, from the safest to the least safe :

  • keyring.<entry> : the value is read from an entry of the keyring of your operating system
  • env.<NAME> : the value is read from an environment variable
  • a hardcoded value, written as is in the file (bad for security)

The prefix decides : a value starting with keyring. is read from the keyring, a value starting with env. from the environment, and any other value is used as it is. A value which merely contains env. or keyring. elsewhere than at the start (a token like glpat-env.something) is a literal.

A sample file

work_dir: /home/johndoe/work/
platforms:
  gitlab.com:
    token: MY_TOKEN # Bad !!
    type: gitlab
    public_key: /path/to/public_key
    public_key_passphrase: env.PUBLIC_KEY_PASSPHRASE
  github.com:
    token: env.ENV_VAR_TOKEN
    type: github

For each platform, you can define the following elements (some can reference an environment variable or the keyring):

Element Description Support env. and keyring. token The authentication token to access the platform ✅ type The type of platform (github, gitlab) ❌ public_key The path to the public key to use for SSH connection ❌ public_key_passphrase The passphrase to use for the public key ✅

public_key_passphrase or public_key_password

public_key_passphrase is the canonical name and the one to use. A first version of Heimdall only read public_key_password, so this one is still accepted. When both are set, public_key_passphrase wins.

docs.title: Keyring
docs.text:
A keyring. reference names an entry of the keyring of your operating system (Keychain on macOS, Secret Service on Linux). The configuration file only holds the name of the entry, never the secret.

Several platforms can point at the same entry, so that a token used by several hosts is rotated in one place :

platforms:
  github.com:
    type: github
    token: keyring.github-token
  github.mycompany.com:
    type: github
    token: keyring.github-token # same entry : one token to rotate
  gitlab.com:
    type: gitlab
    token: keyring.gitlab-token
    public_key_passphrase: keyring.ssh-passphrase

The entries are managed with heimdall credentials, which stores a new secret in the keyring and writes the reference in this file for you.

A token written in the file is plain text on disk

A literal token can be read by anyone, or anything, which can read the file, and ends up in your backups and, if the file is versioned, in its history. heimdall credentials migrate moves the tokens written in the file into the keyring, see credentials.

No keyring ?

The keyring needs a running Secret Service on Linux and is not available on Windows. Without it, the env. references and the literal values keep working, and a keyring. reference resolves to nothing.

docs.title: Morning routine
docs.text:
The commands of your morning routine, run by good-morning and by the M key of the TUI, are defined in the morning_routine element.

morning_routine:
  shell: zsh
  commands: git fetch, git pull
Element Description commands The commands to run in each repository, separated by a comma shell The shell used to run them, bash by default ohmyzsh Set it to true to run them in a login interactive shell (-lic), so that the aliases of your shell are available

docs.title: Credentials : credentials, creds or cred
docs.text:
credentials command checks the tokens of the platforms of your configuration file against their API, and updates the ones which are missing, expired or about to expire.

A new credential is stored in the keyring of your operating system, and the configuration file only keeps a reference to it (keyring.<entry>). Several platforms can share one entry, so that a token used by several hosts is rotated in one place.

Global flags are available too.

A keyring is needed

The keyring needs a running Secret Service (GNOME Keyring, KWallet...) on Linux, and Windows is not supported. Without a keyring, nothing can be stored : use --reference env.MY_VAR to point a platform at an environment variable instead. The platforms configured with env. or a literal value keep working.

Run without any subcommand, heimdall credentials checks every platform, tells what is wrong and offers to fix it.

heimdall credentials

docs.title: List: list or ls
docs.text:
Lists the platforms of the configuration file, with their type, where their token is read from (keyring: name, env: NAME, config file or not set), their SSH key and where its passphrase is read from. Nothing is sent over the network and no secret is ever displayed.

heimdall credentials list

docs.title: Check: check [host...]
docs.text:
Checks the token of every platform, or of the given ones, against its API. Each platform gets a verdict : valid, expiring, rejected, no token, unresolved (the reference points at nothing), unsupported or unreachable.

heimdall credentials check
heimdall credentials check github.com
Flag Description --expiring-within Report a token expiring within this duration, 14 days (336h) by default --quiet or -q Print nothing, only set the exit code --strict Fail when a token is about to expire too

The exit code tells the outcome, so that the command can be used in a script or a cron job :

Code Meaning 0 Everything is fine 1 Something needs fixing : a token is rejected, missing or cannot be resolved. With --strict, a token about to expire too 2 A platform could not be reached, so its token could not be checked 
heimdall credentials check --quiet --strict || echo "Time to rotate a token"

docs.title: Update: update [host...]
docs.text:
Stores a new credential for one or several platforms. Without a host, a list of the platforms is displayed after a check : the ones which need attention are already selected, pick the ones to update with Space.

heimdall credentials update github.com
heimdall credentials update

Heimdall asks for the secret twice, without displaying it, stores it in the keyring and writes the reference in the configuration file. Then it checks the updated platforms again. A host which is not configured yet is accepted, this is how a platform is added : Heimdall asks for its type, or takes it from --type.

Flag Description --all or -a Update every configured platform --entry or -e Name of the keyring entry to store the secret under --from-stdin Read the secret from the standard input instead of asking for it --reference Point the platforms at an existing secret (env.MY_VAR or keyring.my-entry) instead of storing one --ssh-passphrase Update the passphrase of the SSH key instead of the token --type Type of a platform which is not configured yet (github or gitlab)

docs.title: Several platforms at once
docs.text:
When several platforms are chosen, whether picked in the list, given on the command line or with --all, Heimdall asks for one secret, stores it in one keyring entry and points every chosen host at it. The entry is named after the host when there is only one, shared otherwise, or whatever you give with --entry.

heimdall credentials update github.com github.mycompany.com --entry github-token

Both hosts now read keyring.github-token : rotating this token later is one command.

docs.title: Scripting
docs.text:
To store a secret without any prompt, give it on the standard input :

echo "$NEW_TOKEN" | heimdall credentials update github.com --from-stdin

To store nothing and point a platform at an environment variable (the only option without a keyring) :

heimdall credentials update gitlab.com --reference env.GITLAB_TOKEN

docs.title: SSH key passphrase
docs.text:
With --ssh-passphrase, the passphrase of the SSH key is updated instead of the token. There is nothing to check a passphrase against, so no check follows.

heimdall credentials update github.com --ssh-passphrase

docs.title: Migrate: migrate
docs.text:
Moves the tokens written in the configuration file into the keyring : each token is stored in an entry named after its host, and the file keeps a reference to it. Heimdall lists the platforms concerned and asks for a confirmation first.

heimdall credentials migrate

Migrating does not make an exposed token safe

migrate removes a token from the configuration file, but not from your backups, nor from the history of the repository if the file is versioned. A token which was exposed has to be revoked and reissued : use heimdall credentials update for the new one.

docs.title: Env Info : env-info or env
docs.text: This option is useful when you need to provide some information when opening an issue on Heimdall.

docs.title: Global flags
docs.text:
Heimdall provides global flags available for all commands.

You can display options with -h option

docs.title: Config file : --config-file or -f
docs.text:
By default, Heimdall will look for a configuration file in the default config directory with the name heimdall.yml.

You can override this value with this flag to specify the path of your configuration file locally.

heimdall git-info -f /work/heimdall.yml

docs.title: Log directory : --log-dir or -l
docs.text:
By default, Heimdall will write its logs into a file call heimdall.log in the default directory.

You can override this value with this flag to specify the path of your log file locally.

docs.title: Work directory : --work-dir or -w
docs.text:
By default, Heimdall will run in the home directory. You can override this directory in the configuration-file.

But you can also define it at run time with this option. It will override the potential value existing in the configuration file.

docs.title: Verbose mode : --verbose or -v
docs.text: By enabling this option, more logs are traced within the log file and in the console output. This helps to debug if you face some problems running Heimdall.

docs.title: No color mode : --no-color or -n
docs.text: By default, Heimdall will display colored output. If you want to disable this feature, you can use this flag.

docs.title: Git clone : git-clone or gc
docs.text:
git-clone command clone the given URL into a directory that has the same path.

For example, if you want to clone https://github.com/yodamad/heimdall, it will be cloned into <work_dir>/yodamad/heimdall.

Several options are available to customize the created path and global flags are also available.

docs.title: Clone a group: --clone-group or g
docs.text:
With this option, Heimdall will clone all repositories from the given group.

For example, running heimdall git-clone -g https://github.com/yodamad-actions will clone into <work_dir>/yodamad-actions/.

The repositories are cloned one after the other, and each line is numbered so that a group of forty is not a silent wait :

📦 37 repositories to clone
🧬 [1/37] Cloning https://github.com/yodamad-actions/first...
✅ [1/37] https://github.com/yodamad-actions/first cloned
...
🏁 36 cloned, 1 failed

The summary at the end counts what really was cloned : a repository which could not be is counted as failed, and said so on its own line.

With --verbose, the progress of git itself (counting and compressing objects) is displayed too. Cloning a single repository prints what it always printed, without any numbering.

docs.title: Include hostname: --include-hostname or i
docs.text:
Enabling this option will keep in the path created the hostname of the URL to be cloned, removing the suffix from it.

For example, running heimdall git-clone -i https://github.com/yodamad/heimdall will clone into <work_dir>/github/yodamad/heimdall.

docs.title: Keep hostname suffix: --keep-hostname-suffix or k
docs.text:
Enabling this option will keep in the suffix of the hostname of the URL to be cloned.

For example, running heimdall git-clone -i -k https://github.com/yodamad/heimdall will clone into <work_dir>/github.com/yodamad/heimdall.

Warning

The option will be ignored if the --include-hostname option is not set

docs.title: Git Info : git-info or gi
docs.text:
This option helps you with your git repositories. It will list them and tell you if they are up-to-date or not. The command do a local and a remote checks.

Some options are available and described in this page. But there are also global flags available.

While the directories are being searched, the line being refreshed tells how many repositories were found so far and where the search is, 🔍 7 repositories found, scanning ~/work/group. The count grows instead of being an x of y : how many there are is only known once the search is over. Each repository found is kept on a line of its own, so that the search is never a silent wait.

docs.title: Search depth: --depth or -d
docs.text: By default, it searches no more then 3 levels of subdirectories, you can override this with the -d flag.

docs.title: Interactive mode: --interactive-mode or -i
docs.text:
With interactive mode, you can easily: * Pick the folder you want to inspect * Display local changes of a picked folder after analyzing * Display remote commits of a picked folder after analyzing * (soon) Update one or several folders

heimdall git-info -i

docs.title: Good Morning : good-morning or gm
docs.text:
This option will help you run your morning routine on several git repositories quite easily.

Some options are available and described in this page. But there are also global flags available.

The repositories are gone through one after the other, and the line being refreshed tells how far along the routine is, ☀️ [3/12] Good Morning my-repo. Above it, one line is kept per repository already done, ✔ when every command worked and ✖ with the name of the first one which did not. The routine ends with ☕️ All done ! 12 repositories, 2 with a failing command, before the table of the results.

docs.title: Search depth: --depth or -d
docs.text: By default, it searches no more then 3 levels of subdirectories, you can override this with the -d flag.

docs.title: Force mode: --force or -f
docs.text:
By default, heimdall will ask you to confirm before running morning routine. Setting -f flag will force the execution

heimdall good-morning -f

docs.title: Override option: --override-cmds or -o
docs.text:
Set this flag to override the default morning routine command dynamically

heimdall good-morning -o

docs.title: Override commands: --run-cmds or r
docs.text:
Associated with -o, you can set commands to override default morning routine commands

heimdall good-morning -o -r "git status, git pull"

docs.title: TUI : heimdall or tui
docs.text:
Running heimdall without any command (or heimdall tui, heimdall ui) opens a full screen interface to navigate through your git repositories, see their state and run actions on one or several of them.

heimdall -w ~/work

The list shows the repositories found in the work directory as the tree of the folders they are in, like a file navigator : each folder lists its folders, then its repositories, the ones needing attention first. A folder holding nothing but another folder shares its line with it. Next to it are the details of the current repository : what state it is in and what you can do about it, the output of the last commands run on it, its changed files, its incoming and not pushed commits, its branches and its last commits.

On a terminal less than 80 columns wide, the list and the details are displayed one at a time : Tab goes from one to the other.

docs.title: Reading the list
docs.text:
Above the list, the header tells how many repositories are in each state, and the colored band below it shows the share of each of them, the most urgent on the left. On the right is the directory Heimdall is looking in or, while actions are running, how many of them are done.

Each repository is listed with the branch it is on, when there is room for it, and its state.

The state of each repository is written in plain words on its right, in a color telling how urgent it is.

Color State Red Diverged from origin, or the repository can't be read Orange Behind origin Yellow Local changes Teal Commits not pushed Green Up to date Grey Nothing to do, but it can't be told to be up to date : no remote, branch not on origin, or last fetch more than a day old

While an action is running on a repository, its state is replaced by what is being done. Then the result of the action is displayed instead, until the next one.

The line at the bottom of the screen always shows the last thing Heimdall did, so that a run on many repositories is never silent : the header keeps the count of how many are done, the bottom line says what just happened. Press Shift+L for the whole history.

No network at startup

To be displayed quickly, the list is built from local information only, so what it knows about origin dates from the last fetch. When this fetch is more than a day old, the details tell its age : press F to check origin.

The other commands (git-info, git-clone, good-morning, env-info) are still available for a non-interactive usage.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Key Action Up / Down or J / K Move G / Shift+G or Home / End First / last repository Page Up / Page Down Previous / next page Tab Go to the details, Tab again to go back Enter Collapse / expand the folder Left or H Collapse the folder, or go to the folder the line is in Right or L Expand the folder, or go into it Z Collapse / expand all the folders / Filter repositories by path Esc Clear the filter, then the selection ? Help Q Quit

docs.title: Selection
docs.text:
Actions are run on the selected repositories or, if none is selected, on the current one. With the cursor on a folder, they are run on all its repositories, the ones of the folders it holds included.

A collapsed folder tells what its repositories need, and the details list them all by state, the ones needing attention first. When the list is scrolled, its first line tells the whole path of the folder the next ones are in.

Key Action Space Select / unselect the current repository, or all the ones of the current folder A Select / unselect all the displayed repositories U Select the repositories which can be pulled

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
A confirmation is asked before pulling or running commands on several repositories.

Key Action R Refresh local status F git fetch P git pull, skipped for repositories with local changes M Run the morning routine defined in the configuration file ! Run a command C Open the credentials screen Shift+L Show the activity log

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
Press C to open the credentials screen. It shows one line per platform of the configuration file : where its token comes from (the keyring, an environment variable or the file itself, never the token) and the verdict of its API : valid, expiring, rejected, no token...

Nothing is checked until you ask

Consistent with the no network at startup promise above, no credential is checked when Heimdall starts. The platforms are checked when you open this screen with C, and again with R.

Key Action Up / Down or J / K Move Space Select / unselect a platform A Select / unselect all the platforms Enter Update the credential of the selected platforms, or of the current one when none is selected R Check the platforms again Esc Back to the list

Updating asks for the name of a keyring entry, then for the secret, which is never displayed. Several selected platforms share one entry, so that a token used by several of them is rotated once. The same operations, and more, are available from the command line with credentials.

When a fetch or a pull fails because of a credential, the message tells which platform and what is wrong (token, SSH key or passphrase), and offers C to fix it, with this platform already selected.

docs.title: Activity
docs.text: Fetching or pulling forty repositories takes a while, and only six of them run at a time. To tell what is going on, Heimdall keeps what it did and shows it in three places : the last line is always at the bottom of the screen, a panel takes over while an action runs on several repositories, and Shift+L opens the whole history, newest at the bottom.

docs.title: While a run is going on
docs.text:
One line cannot say much about forty repositories, so a panel docks under the list for the length of the run. Its top edge is the progress of the run, read as the band under the header : how many repositories are done, how many hold one of the six workers, and how many wait for one. Under it :

  • how far along the run is, how many repositories are running and queued, how many have failed and how long it has been going on,
  • one line per repository being worked on, each with the last thing git said about it, which is where the percentages of a long clone or pull are seen,
  • the failures of this run, marked with a ✖, so that the one repository which asked for a password is not lost among the thirty-nine which went fine.

The panel takes its lines from the list, never more than half of the pane, and goes away once the run is over. On a short terminal there is no room for it : the count stays in the header and the last line at the bottom of the screen.

docs.title: The whole history
docs.text:
Key Action Shift+L Show the activity, Esc or Shift+L again to go back Up / Down or J / K, Page Up / Page Down Scroll Shift+G or End Follow the last lines again, after scrolling away

Each line tells when it happened, which repository it is about and what happened, warnings and errors being marked with a ⚠ and a ✖ so that they are told apart with --no-color too. The details of a repository end with a Recent activity section listing the last lines about it alone.

More detail with -v

Reading the local status of a repository happens for all of them at startup and again after every action, so those lines are only shown with the --verbose flag. The same lines are always written to the log file, whatever the flags : see --log-dir.

docs.title: Branches
docs.text:
When a repository has several local branches, the details list them : the one the repository is on first, marked with a star, then the most recently committed ones. Each tells where it stands compared to origin and how old its last commit is, so that work left on a branch which was never pushed is not forgotten.

Press Tab to go to the details, then :

Key Action Up / Down or J / K Choose a branch, or scroll the details when there is only one Enter Switch to the chosen branch with git switch Page Up / Page Down Scroll the details Tab or Esc Go back to the list

When git refuses to switch, because of local changes for instance, the details tell why.

docs.title: Search depth: --depth or -d
docs.text:
By default, it searches no more than 3 levels of subdirectories, you can override this with the -d flag of the tui command.

heimdall tui -d 5

docs.title: Global flags
docs.text: The global flags are available too. With --no-color, the states are told by their text only and the colored band is not displayed.
